## Сохранённая техническая постановка и история

## What
Add bin/pm-reminders-push: a bash wrapper that runs pm ingest --source task for hyperide, computes pm reminders, and pushes one Telegram digest via tg when reminders are non-empty (silent exit 0 otherwise). Wire it into crontab (3 times per day).

## Why (motivation)
Stuck or overdue tickets in the pm work queue need to surface to the CTO without manual polling.

## User impact
The CTO gets a Telegram nudge when tickets are blocked, stale, duplicated, cycling, or past an SLA timer, instead of tickets silently rotting unseen.

## Cost of inaction
Stuck or duplicate work items across projects go unnoticed indefinitely; the pm reminders engine already built has no delivery path to a human.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] pm ingest --source task --repo-dir <hyperide> completes without hanging and produces new work items
- [ ] pm reminders --json returns an empty array or a list of reminder objects
- [ ] the wrapper script exits 0 silently when reminders are empty
- [ ] the wrapper script sends exactly one tg --format html digest (capped at 10 items plus a remaining count) when reminders are non-empty
- [ ] crontab has one new line invoking the wrapper 3 times per day without clobbering existing entries

## User impact
The person reading the weekly digest message on Telegram sees a line like "Throughput (7d): shipped 5 - item A, item B, ..." and reasonably reads that as five things shipped this week. The weekly digest keeps silently overcounting throughput indefinitely; every consumer of that number is misled every week, and the gap only gets less visible as it becomes accepted as how the number has always looked.

- [ ] pm report monthly's pre-existing shipped section at pmlib/reports.py:290 (same _SHIPPED_STATES pattern) is either fixed in the same change or explicitly filed as a separate follow-up ticket, so the same undeployed-counted-as-shipped bug is not left live in a second surface.
